compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.hw_notes: RTX5090Mobile (Blackwell-class) with tensor cores. fp16 MMA via tl.dot. Window N=16, head dim C=32, hidden=128, image 720x1280.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.notes: Most ops are small-matmul-heavy with tiny N=16; tensor cores underutilized unless we fuse multiple windows into a tile dimension. MLP fc1/fc2 (32->128->32) per pixel is the heaviest cost.
compute_intensity_and_hw_fit.risk: Small inner dim (32) keeps tensor core utilization low; need to fuse over batch/spatial.

memory_bandwidth.notes: Input is 1x720x1280x32 fp16 = ~58MB. Multiple round-trips between LN/attn/MLP dominate. Full fusion of (LN1->attn->residual->LN2->MLP->residual) can save several full-tensor reads/writes.
memory_bandwidth.risk: Weight matrices (qkv 32x96, proj 32x32, fc1 32x128, fc2 128x32) are tiny (~50KB total) and fit in shared/registers easily.

register_pressure.notes: Per-window working set: 16 tokens x 32 channels = 512 fp16 values, plus 128-hidden MLP intermediate = 16x128 = 2048 fp16. Manageable per CTA.
register_pressure.risk: If we try to keep entire windows + MLP hidden in registers, may exceed budget; shared memory staging is fine.

nodes.notes:
1) CLASSIFICATION: Mixed kernel — LayerNorm (reduction), windowed self-attention (small-matmul + softmax), residual add, LayerNorm, MLP (two GEMMs + GELU), residual add. Window=4x4=16 tokens, C=32, num_heads=1, mlp_ratio=4 -> hidden=128. Input (1,720,1280,32) fp16. nH=180, nW=320 -> 57600 windows. 2) MATH: y=x+Proj(Softmax(QK^T/sqrt(C)+rpe)V) on LN1(x); y=y+fc2(GELU(fc1(LN2(y)))). All reductions are per-token (LN over C=32) or per-window (softmax over N=16). 3) LAYOUT: Input NHWC, weights small enough to live in shared mem / constant. Window partition is a reshape/permute — can be expressed by index math. RPE bias (1,1,16,16)=256 fp16 constants. 4) REGIMES: (a) Memory-bound full-pipeline traversal — likely dominant due to ~58MB tensor traversed many times in reference. (b) Compute-bound on MLP if fused (32x128 matmul x 921600 tokens ≈ 7.5 GFLOPs fp16 — small). (c) Small-matmul attention regime where tensor cores underutilized for N=16. 5) KNOBS: per-CTA = one window (16 tokens) or block of windows; staging of QKV/proj/fc1/fc2 in shared; whether to fuse attn+MLP or split; tl.dot with BLOCK_M>=16; vectorized loads on C=32 (one float4 per token). 6) SKELETON: Grid over windows (and possibly groups of windows). Each CTA: load 16x32 tile, apply LN1, compute QKV via tl.dot using shared weights, compute attn (16x16) + softmax + V proj (16x32), apply proj linear, add residual, LN2, fc1 (16x128), GELU, fc2 (16x32), add residual, store. 7) FAMILIES: F1 (TOP) Full-fusion single kernel — entire block per window CTA; working set: x(16x32=1KB)+hidden(16x128=4KB)+weights(qkv=6KB, proj=2KB, fc1=8KB, fc2=8KB)+rpe(0.5KB) ≈ 30KB shared, fits easily. Strength: one HBM read + one HBM write of activations. Weakness: weight broadcast to every CTA (cached in L2 ~50KB, fine). F2 Two-kernel split: attn-fused-kernel then MLP-fused-kernel, simpler but extra round-trip of 58MB. F3 Hybrid: fuse LN+attn+proj+residual+LN2 first, then fc1+GELU+fc2+residual, sharing nothing — same drawback as F2. Choose F1.

Key constraints: num_heads=1, shift=(0,0), window=4x4, dim=32, hidden=128, fp16 throughout. LN uses fp32 accumulation. RPE is a learned constant buffer.

action.description: Implement a single Triton kernel that processes one (or a small group of) 4x4 window per program. The kernel loads the 16x32 tile, runs LN1, computes QKV via tl.dot with weights cached from shared memory, performs 16x16 attention with RPE + softmax, multiplies by V, applies output projection, adds the residual, runs LN2, fc1 (32->128) + GELU + fc2 (128->32), adds the second residual, and stores back. Weights are loaded once per CTA from globals (relying on L2 reuse).
action.rationale: Eliminates ~5 full-tensor round trips through HBM (LN1 out, qkv out, attn out, proj out, LN2 out, fc1 out, fc2 out). Working set fits in shared memory. Tensor cores can be used for fc1/fc2 by grouping multiple windows along M.

kernel_summary: Simplified Swin transformer block in fp16 over a (1,720,1280,32) NHWC tensor with 4x4 non-shifted windows, single head, dim=32, mlp_ratio=4 (hidden=128). The block is LayerNorm -> windowed self-attention (QKV linear, scaled dot-product with relative position bias, softmax, V multiply, output projection) + residual -> LayerNorm -> MLP (fc1 32->128, GELU, fc2 128->32) + residual. The reference issues many small ops, traversing the 58MB activation tensor multiple times through HBM, and the small inner dims (C=32, N=16) make tensor cores underutilized in vendor kernels. The kernel is primarily memory-bandwidth bound at the block level and small-matmul/tensor-core-utilization bound at the op level. Key constraints: num_heads=1, shift=(0,0), window=[4,4], weights are tiny (~50KB total) and fit in shared memory, LN must accumulate mean/var in fp32 for fp16 stability, RPE bias is a constant (1,1,16,16) buffer. The biggest performance lever is fusing the entire block into a single Triton kernel so activations stay on-chip; the second lever is grouping multiple windows per program to raise tl.dot tile sizes for tensor cores.
open_questions: What is the exact register budget on RTX5090Mobile per Triton program, and at what BLOCK_M does the fully-fused kernel begin to spill?
Can we group adjacent windows along nW to keep window-partitioned tokens contiguous in memory, avoiding scatter/gather, given the (B,nH,Wh,nW,Ww,C) reshape?
Is fp16 sufficient for softmax accumulation across N=16, or do we need fp32 max/sum to match reference tolerance?
Does folding LN affine into the next Linear cause unacceptable fp16 drift relative to the reference (which keeps LN affine separate)?
What tolerance is used for correctness checking — does it accept fp16-internal MLP matmuls or require fp32 accumulation in tl.dot?
Is torch.compile's baseline already fusing LN+attn or LN+MLP via inductor — i.e., what is the realistic baseline latency to beat?
Should the kernel be one program per window (57600 programs) or grouped (e.g., 14400 programs of 4 windows) for best occupancy on RTX5090Mobile?
Are the weights guaranteed contiguous in the expected layout, and can we transpose qkv weights once at init to maximize coalesced loads inside the kernel?
